transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that I keep dodging anything that even smells like my old job. Office buildings, security talks, networking events near the work sites... I just stay away from all of it. And if people start asking me about the day it happened, I just make some excuse and get out of there. I decided to come in because it's just becoming too much to work around.
Do you ever find yourself reliving the day it happened, like it's happening all over again?

Yes, I do. It just... it happens out of nowhere, really. I'll be doing something completely normal, like washing the dishes, or driving past a warehouse gate, and the scene just pops right back into my head. 

It's so sharp. I can actually hear the panic in people's voices, and my chest tightens up... it really feels exactly like I'm right back there when it happens.
Do you try to avoid thinking about what happened?

Yeah, I really do. Like I mentioned when we first started talking, that's the main reason I keep dodging anything to do with my old job. I stay away from the office buildings, the networking events near the sites... all of it, really, just so I don't have to think about it. And if someone actually brings up that day and starts asking questions, I just make an excuse and leave. I try my hardest to just push it out of my mind.
Do you have trouble sleeping?

Yes, I do. Most nights I just lie there... I'm exhausted, but I'm completely wired, you know? And when I finally do fall asleep, I end up waking up from these dreams. It's always the sound of radios crackling, or people shouting. Once that wakes me up, I'm up for good, usually way before the sun comes up. I just feel like I never really get any rest.
Do you have difficulty concentrating?

No, not really. I mean, I'm definitely tired during the day because of the sleep issues I just mentioned, but my focus itself is fine. I haven't noticed any real trouble concentrating on things when I need to get them done.
Do you find yourself jumping or startled by loud noises or unexpected movements?

Yes, definitely. If a car backfires outside, or a door slams... or even if somebody just touches my shoulder when I don't see them coming, I jump really hard. And it takes a while to calm down. My heart just keeps racing long after everyone else has moved on and forgotten about it.
Do you always feel like you're on the lookout for something to happen, even when you're in a safe place?

Yes, I do. It's like I can't turn it off. Whenever I walk into a room—like a meeting room at work, or even just a restaurant—the first thing I do is look for the exits. I just... I need to know where they are. And I always watch people's hands. I make sure to pick a seat against the wall, so nobody can come up behind me. I just can't relax unless I know exactly what's going on around me.
Do you feel guilty or responsible for what happened that day?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I know it wasn't my fault. I don't feel like I caused it or that I should have done something differently. It just... it just happened.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms?
This has been going on since... well, since I was fired right after that armed incident. So it's been about a year and seven months now.
Have you avoided any activities or places that you used to enjoy before the incident?

Yes, I have. Actually, that's a big part of what brings me in. I just keep dodging anything that even smells like that old job. Office buildings, security talks, networking events near work sites... I just stay away from all of it. And if I'm out and people start asking about the day it happened, I just... I make some excuse and get out of there. I really can't be around it.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy doing before the incident?

No, I wouldn't say I've lost interest in things I enjoy. I mean, I still like my hobbies and spending time with my family, things like that. It's really just the work-related stuff and talking about the incident that I try to avoid. But my normal interests outside of that... those are still the same.
Do you feel constantly on edge, like something bad is about to happen, even when there's no apparent reason to feel that way?

Yes, I do. It's... well, whenever I walk into a meeting room or a restaurant, the very first thing I do is notice the exits. I find myself watching people’s hands, just to see what they're doing, and I always make sure to pick a seat where nobody can come up behind me. I just can't seem to turn that alert off, even when I know I'm safe.
Have you avoided forming close relationships with others because of what happened?

I wouldn't say I actively avoid people, but things definitely feel different now. I still show up sometimes for family gatherings, or for mentoring some of the younger folks, things like that. But... I just feel disconnected. It's like I'm sitting behind a pane of glass. I'm there, nodding along and listening, but it feels like everybody else is actually together and I'm just... somewhere else entirely.
Have you stopped doing any important activities because of your avoidance?

Yes, I have. I've actually turned down interviews lately, and I've stopped taking on my usual volunteer responsibilities. I just can’t reliably get through meetings or site visits anymore without shutting down or having to leave. And even with my family and those mentoring circles I mentioned... I’m just less present. People have started noticing it, too. They can see that I pull back now, instead of stepping up and leading like I used to.
Have you avoided any social activities because of your experiences?

No, not really. I mean, I don't stay home just to avoid social events. I still go to family dinners or get-togethers if I'm invited. So, no, I wouldn't say I avoid them outright... I just kind of sit there quietly when I do go, like I was saying before.
